title: the-pulse-file-is-the-subscription
intention: The ground loop serves any component's per-beat work by discovering groundloop/pulse.py at the component's own address (class or instance level) each pass — presence activates the service, absence deactivates and unloads it; nothing registers, nothing restarts.
why: Akien, 2026-08-15, verbatim: 'devices/webserver/groundloop/pulse.py will be our webserver's shim's pulse. so i'm the group loop and i am already running and i look in that folder. last time i was here, pulse.py did not exist. so inside a try/except i can either run it, or i can import it. either way, once i activeate it, it's now in my list of things i know about.... next pass thru, the file is missing. so i remove it from my list. if i imported it, i now unload it. this is true for every device. a goundloop folder can exist at the class level or the instance level. nobody has to do anything except put the file there or remove it. so this keeps the ground loop from needing a restart, from getting stale, from anybody needing to do anything other than just use the provided service or not.' The lived symptom: on 2026-08-14 the loop measured itself older than the code it judges nine times overnight and nothing owned a restart — under this design there is no restart to own, because the loop holds nothing that ages: its picture of the rack is rebuilt from disk every beat.
traces_to: Law 4 (the file's existence IS the subscription — physics, not a list anyone maintains), Law 1 (registration compiled into the address, never re-derived), Law 6 (the pulse berths at the device's own address and fires through the device's shim; the loop owns only its beat and its learned list). Up the ruled ladder (2026-08-07): the ground loop running is rung 1 of everything-below-is-working-fine.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariants: proved by the tester running proofs beside the code that a hollow build could not pass (run twice, never trust the first green), feeds back to origin on failure. IN: discovery gains the groundloop/pulse.py surface at class and instance level (found each beat, activated under try/except, identity path+mtime, removed+unloaded when missing); firing routed through the shim (the loop only beats); the learned list is loop-owned instance state; the charter's subscription sentence updated (write pokes recompile_gate.sh); proofs for add, remove, in-place edit, and a pulse that raises. OUT: the resident interpreter's own staleness (measured separately, its own concern); the beat overspend (cast ticket exists); migrating or changing the existing probes/ surface; building any real device's pulse content (the webserver's pulse is the webserver's work).
falsifier.proves_red: With the loop running and untouched (same pid throughout): drop a pulse.py under a component's groundloop/ folder → it is activated and fired within one beat; remove it → within one beat it stops firing and leaves the learned list; edit it in place → the next beat runs the new bytes (identity is path+mtime, so an edit is a remove+add in one act). Any of those requiring a loop restart, a hand-maintained list, or a registration act falsifies the intent. Horizon: one build, bounded to the discovery+unload seam; no device's actual pulse content is in scope.
falsifier.horizon: One build, bounded to the discovery+unload seam of the ground loop. No device's actual pulse content is in scope; the webserver's pulse is the webserver's own later work.
